steps.title: Technology in sport
steps.body: The use of scientific and digital innovations to improve officiating decisions, enhance performance, advance equipment design, and increase safety. Technology has transformed sport at every level, from grassroots to elite competition.

steps.title: Balanced View
steps.body: Technology has significantly improved accuracy, safety and performance in sport. However, it has also introduced new problems including cost inequality, delays and a diminished human element. The key challenge is finding the right balance between using technology to support sport and allowing it to dominate sport.

steps.title: PE Exam Tips — Technology in Sport
steps.body: 1. For Technology in Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Technology in Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give both positive AND negative impacts when discussing technology Use specific named technologies (Hawk-Eye, VAR, GPS) not just "technology" Address each stakeholder group separately - performers, officials, coaches, spectators Know the difference between VAR (review system) and GLT (instant automated decision) The swimming suit ban is a great example of technology going too far Evaluate: don't just list impacts - weigh up whether technology is overall positive or negative
